vignette: A 74-year-old woman after cardiac arrest can read single letters but not words, reaches past objects she looks at, and describes a picture of a kitchen one item at a time without grasping the scene. Acuity is normal.
explanation: Simultanagnosia, optic ataxia and ocular apraxia form Balint syndrome, from bilateral dorsal parieto-occipital damage; after cardiac arrest the lesions lie in the border zones between the middle and posterior cerebral arteries, the superior lateral occipital and superior parietal cortex.
